audits.title: 700 Audit on Antibiotic Prescriptions in Neuro-Rehabilitation Wards (C2 And L1) Of Salford Royal Foundation Trust
audits.standard: Trust antibiotic guidelines
audits.setting: Neuro-rehabilitation wards C2 and L1, Salford Royal Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 45 prescriptions; indication documented in 95%; 100% for allergy status and course length; 53.4% met clinical criteria; 52.3% of those not meeting criteria discussed with microbiology or a senior.

audits.intervention: not reported
audits.other_findings: UTIs accounted for 37.8% of prescriptions.

audits.title: 725 Monthly Antibiotic Use in The Sheffield Children’s Hospital ED: A Hospital-Based Clinical Audit
audits.standard: Local ED antibiotic guidelines
audits.setting: Emergency Department, Sheffield Children's Hospital

cycle1.result: 88% of antibiotic prescribing appropriate; 12 prescribed inappropriately (co-amoxiclav 41.7%, penicillin V 25%, amoxicillin and flucloxacillin 16.7% each).

audits.intervention: not reported

audits.title: AN AUDIT OF THE PAEDIATRIC EMPIRIC ANTI-INFECTIVE GUIDELINES AND ANTI-INFECTIVE DRUG DOSE TABLE FOR CHILDREN.
audits.standard: Local paediatric empiric anti-infective guidelines and drug dose table: 90% adherence to empirical guidelines; 90% indication recorded; 90% duration/review date recorded; 95% initial doses adhere to dose table
audits.setting: Paediatric wards, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 40/41 (98%) adhered to empirical guidelines; 40/42 (95%) had indication stated; 26/42 (62%) had duration/review date recorded; 67/69 (97%) initial doses adhered to dose table.

audits.intervention: Proposed only: present results to stewardship and pharmacy teams, electronic prescribing with mandatory fields, update antibiotic smartphone app, compulsory junior doctor education.
audits.other_findings: Previous audit in 2013 showed 72% guideline adherence, 16% indication recording and 14% duration recording, so all improved; duration documentation still failed the standard.
audits.citation: Zaffar S, Fletcher P. AN AUDIT OF THE PAEDIATRIC EMPIRIC ANTI-INFECTIVE GUIDELINES AND ANTI-INFECTIVE DRUG DOSE TABLE FOR CHILDREN. Arch Dis Child. 2016;101(9):e2. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.15. PMID: 27540193.

audits.title: P39 Start smart: improving the quality of empiric antimicrobial prescribing at a tertiary paediatric hospital
audits.standard: Local antimicrobial guidelines: ≥90% of children admitted via ED and started on antibiotics have a documented indication and guideline-compliant choice
audits.setting: Emergency department admissions, tertiary paediatric hospital

cycle1.result: Documentation of indication and guideline compliance median 30%.

audits.intervention: Weekly audit feedback with run charts, antibiotic discussion at Monday handover, prescriber spot quiz, updated guidelines and prescribing app, ID badge guideline cards, and reminders at point of prescribing in ED.

cycle2.result: Documentation of indication and guideline compliance 100% consistently.

audits.other_findings: Weekly audits sampled the first ten children admitted via ED on antibiotics; improvement persisted through three NCHD changeovers. Antimicrobial expenditure fell by €101,078.44 from 2014 to 2015.
audits.citation: Kirrane M, Cunney R, McNamara R, Okafor I. P39 Start smart: improving the quality of empiric antimicrobial prescribing at a tertiary paediatric hospital. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2018;103(2):e2.43-e2. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2017-314585.48.

audits.title: P06 Improving antibiotic prescribing practice in a tertiary burns and plastic surgery department
audits.standard: Updated local plastic surgery infection guidelines
audits.setting: Tertiary burns and plastic surgery department

cycle1.result: Prescriber compliance with the guideline 50%

audits.intervention: Guideline updated using local resistance data, departmental teaching, appropriate antibiotics made available in burns and plastics theatres, and all guidelines combined into one document

cycle2.result: Prescriber compliance 71% after three intervention cycles

audits.other_findings: Co-amoxiclav and clindamycin were the most common non-compliant prescriptions, reflecting historical usage.
audits.citation: . P06 Improving antibiotic prescribing practice in a tertiary burns and plastic surgery department. JAC Antimicrob Resist. 2023;5(Suppl 2).

audits.title: 150. Using audit-and-feedback to improve antibiotic-prescribing in Emergency Departments: a quasi-experimental study across 4 sites in the Veterans Health Administration
audits.standard: Guideline-concordant management of 5 acute respiratory infections and cystitis
audits.setting: 2 intervention and 2 control emergency departments, Veterans Health Administration

cycle1.result: Guideline-concordant management 52.1%.

audits.intervention: One-to-one education and individualised quarterly feedback on antibiotic prescribing with peer comparison.

cycle2.result: Guideline-concordant management 72.2%; antibiotic use fell 8.9% vs 3.4% at control sites (RRR -3.3%, 95% CI -8.4 to +1.7).

audits.other_findings: Overall antibiotic use did not fall significantly compared with control EDs.
audits.citation: Livorsi D, Nair R, Dysangco A, Aylward A, Alexander B, Smith M, et al.. 150. Using audit-and-feedback to improve antibiotic-prescribing in Emergency Departments: a quasi-experimental study across 4 sites in the Veterans Health Administration. Open Forum Infect Dis. 2020;7(Suppl 1):S85-S85.

audits.title: Audit of an antibiotic policy and microbiological investigations for treating bacteraemia in a large teaching hospital.
audits.standard: Hospital antibiotic policy for empirical therapy
audits.setting: Aberdeen Royal Infirmary, large teaching hospital

cycle1.result: Poor use of the antibiotic policy, with inadequate (P=0.005) or excessive (P<0.00001) antibiotic treatment and a trend to increased mortality.

audits.intervention: not reported
audits.other_findings: 87% of blood cultures were Gram-stain positive within 24 h, but streamlined therapy was still judged excessive in 27%.

audits.title: Clinical audit of linezolid use in a large teaching hospital.
audits.standard: Hospital antibiotic committee indications for linezolid use, including prior infection specialist approval
audits.setting: Ninewells Hospital, Dundee (teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance with local recommendations very good; only 34 of 77 had documented prior approval by an infection specialist.

audits.intervention: Mandatory linezolid order form to be completed by the prescriber (future evaluation planned).
audits.other_findings: Main justifications were renal dysfunction or poor venous access (34%) and glycopeptide intolerance or failure (32%); MRSA was the commonest proven pathogen (56%).

audits.setting: Point prevalence survey in four acute teaching hospitals using the ESAC audit tool

audits.standard: National clinical practice guideline for antibiotic use in community-acquired pneumonia and acute exacerbations of COPD
audits.setting: Respiratory medicine department, University Hospital of North Norway

cycle1.result: Appropriate empirical antibiotics prescribed in 61.7%.

audits.title: Practice implications of an antimicrobial stewardship intervention in a tertiary care teaching hospital, Qatar.
audits.standard: National antibiotic prescribing guidelines
audits.setting: Tertiary care teaching hospital (National Center for Cancer Care and Research), Doha

cycle1.result: 60% of prescriptions complied with guidelines; rationale for non-adherence not documented in 37.2% of cases.

audits.intervention: Educational intervention using PDSA targeting suboptimal documentation.

cycle2.result: Slight improvement in documentation (figures not reported).

audits.other_findings: Febrile neutropenia was the commonest indication (20.7%) and carbapenems the commonest class (21.4%); interviews identified facilitators and barriers.

audits.title: Impact of implementing repeated clinical audits and feedback on outpatient antibiotic prescribing in the pediatric emergency department of a French university hospital.
audits.standard: French scientific society antibiotic guidelines
audits.setting: Paediatric emergency department, University Hospital of Nancy

cycle1.result: Overall guideline adherence 75%; 51.6% where antibiotics recommended; treatment initiation 88.9%; appropriate antibiotic choice 82.2%.

audits.intervention: Repeated audits with regular prescriber meetings, educational sessions and rapid feedback.

cycle2.result: Overall adherence stable; 50% where antibiotics recommended; initiation 96.6%; appropriate choice 93.2% (p = 0.001).

audits.other_findings: 1477 prescriptions retained; antibiotic consumption fell.
audits.citation: Ben Yaghlane M, Florentin A, Pereira O, Borsa-Dorion A, Schweitzer C, Charmillon A. Impact of implementing repeated clinical audits and feedback on outpatient antibiotic prescribing in the pediatric emergency department of a French university hospital. Arch Pediatr. 2026;33(3):105476. doi:10.1016/j.arcped.2026.01.002. PMID: 41622049.
